alternatives.mechanism: Implement a mobile app that uses the device camera to scan barcodes or capture ingredient photos, applying computer‑vision models to auto‑extract item names and estimate expiration dates, supplemented by a crowdsourced verification step where users confirm or correct the inferred data.
addresses_issues: User-provided pantry and expiration data may be inaccurate or incomplete
Generated meal suggestions may not be appealing or practical for users
Measuring food waste before and after the intervention is challenging
tradeoffs: Requires users to have a smartphone with camera and internet access
Adds development complexity and higher app maintenance costs
Potential privacy concerns around image capture
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Combines AI‑driven visual recognition with community validation to improve data accuracy and enrich suggestion relevance.

alternatives.mechanism: Create a gamified platform where users earn points for logging their pantry inventory, rating suggested meals, and uploading photos of leftover or discarded food after cooking; the system uses these self‑reported waste images to quantify waste reduction and refines future suggestions based on community ratings.
addresses_issues: User-provided pantry and expiration data may be inaccurate or incomplete
Generated meal suggestions may not be appealing or practical for users
Measuring food waste before and after the intervention is challenging
tradeoffs: Relies on user motivation to consistently log waste data, which may introduce reporting bias
Increases user interaction time, potentially reducing adoption
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Introduces game mechanics and visual waste logging to turn data collection into an engaging activity, improving measurement fidelity.

alternatives.mechanism: Partner with grocery retailers to obtain anonymized purchase histories for participating households, using typical shelf‑life tables to infer pantry stock and expiration windows; the system then generates meal suggestions based on these inferred inventories and tracks waste by comparing purchased quantities to reported consumption.
addresses_issues: User-provided pantry and expiration data may be inaccurate or incomplete
Generated meal suggestions may not be appealing or practical for users
Measuring food waste before and after the intervention is challenging
tradeoffs: Depends on retailer cooperation and data‑sharing agreements
May be less personalized than direct user entry, leading to less optimal suggestions
Raises privacy considerations regarding purchase data
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Leverages external purchase data to auto‑populate pantry information, reducing user entry burden and providing a baseline for waste measurement.
